0.content:
When the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat from the sea of stars and fought the Seven Sovereigns, they made four Shades from themselves: Life, Death (Ronova), Time (Istaroth) and Space (Asmoday). Shades avoid being named by the living and work under Celestia's rules. They can lend fragments of their power: Ronova lent hers to Xbalanque, and Istaroth lent hers to Barbatos.

In the official teaser "The Gods' Limits" (2025-07-09), Ronova, Rhinedottir and Istaroth search a ruined space for the missing Asmoday. Ronova says that since the Shades were cast, none of them has ever missed a meeting. She cannot believe a Shade would switch sides unless she loved a new master more than herself. Istaroth warns her she is being watched, and Ronova finds Pierro's gaze from Nod-Krai. She mocks the Cryo Archon's "paltry powers". With no direct order to act, she proposes that they intervene, within what the "rules" permit.

In 6.6 Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius appeared to Nahida when she invoked her authority to burn Irminsul. Ronova asked whether Nahida truly meant to abandon the root of everything she had fought for, and the Shades let her proceed. In 7.1 Naberius and Rhinedottir both speak for Life, and Rhinedottir says Celestia watches them closely as Ronova's likely accomplices.

1.comment: Ronova: Xbalanque's Pact and Natlan's Rules
1.content:
After the war of funerary flame shattered Natlan's Ley Lines, Ronova had the Lord of the Night build the Night Kingdom to repair them and guide souls. The Heavenly Principles censured her for overstepping. Later the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, demanded more than courage for his people. She wrote Natlan's rules into the Night Kingdom and agreed to lend her power, warning that it carried a deadly price. If its wielder could not master the fear of death, innocents would die in their place. She called herself "merely a Shade" with little freedom, told him to keep the deal secret, and said she would blame him for stealing her power if questioned.

The rules let ordinary humans become Pyro Archon through the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Xbalanque also asked to see Natlan's future if its people prevailed against the Abyss. After Natlan won, she let him return for one day in Mausau's body during Mavuika's story quest (5.3). He offered Mavuika the rest of the life force Ronova had given him, and she declined.

2.comment: Ronova: Mavuika's Debt and Capitano's Paradox
2.content:
Mavuika used Ronova's power to drive back the Abyss, and by the rules her death was owed. At ruined Ochkanatlan, Ronova's eyes opened in the sky. She said she had grown weary of waiting and no longer cared what became of the land, yet she praised the people for meeting the Heavenly Principles' expectations, and announced she would witness Mavuika's death. Capitano offered himself instead. Because Ronova's own Curse of Immortality kept him from dying, his death would create a paradox. Rather than break the curse, Ronova let it stand. His life force passed to the Lord of the Night, and Mavuika lived.

Capitano had already named her in 5.2 as the source of his people's suffering, removing his mask to show what the curse had done to his face. He said the Ruler of Death can freely define death or grant immortality to anyone she chooses, but that no rule is unbreakable. At Ochkanatlan she grumbled that her duties had become cumbersome and that she might lose her patience. In the end she conceded, in effect, that he had used her own rules against her.

3.content:
During the cataclysm 500 years ago, Ronova cursed the pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality, making no distinction between the Five Sinners or the king and the innocent majority. The curse slowly erodes body and soul. Pierro, Capitano and Dainsleif carry it, and each holds her responsible.

The teaser "The Gods' Limits" shows the young Pierro glaring up at her as she cast it, and she still remembers his eyes. Dainsleif says that when the Khaenri'ahns looked up at her then, they saw an untouchable god. In 7.1 the Traveler reasons that this curse was placed under the Heavenly Principles' judgement and is permanent, beyond even her power to lift. That is why it outlasted her Curse of Death.

The curse kept turning against her: it gave Capitano his paradox in Natlan, and it let Pierro wake early from her Curse of Death at the Armory Palace ("The curse of immortality is stubborn").

4.comment: Ronova: The Curse of Death over Snezhnaya
4.content:
To stop Snezhnaya threatening the Heavenly Principles, Ronova laid a curse on the nation. Anyone who conceived such an advance died, along with everyone near them, then revived with no memory of the idea. Researchers at the Armory Palace reported strange memory loss, and Project Mistilteinn stalled. Killing humans this way broke Celestia's rules, so Rhinedottir revived the victims within a window before each monitoring cycle could notice.

In a recorded memory the Traveler revisits in 7.1, Rhinedottir warns that death is not a power to abuse and that punishing humans without the Heavenly Principles' approval is a grave sin. Ronova replies that during the slumber, Celestia only checks on them periodically. She also said a reckoning would come for Snezhnaya once the Heavenly Principles woke. When she lost her authority the curse ended, because she had imposed it on her own initiative.

5.content:
Mitya's inspiration during Odette's rehearsal triggered the curse, and the whole theater died. Long ago, angels had altered the theater's Ley Lines to hold the souls of "special creations", and now they accepted only two ordinary souls a day. The dead experienced a blizzard trapping them inside. Two lingering dead, Shram and Ptashka, had resisted the Ley Lines for centuries, and their accumulated resentment was, in Ronova's word, a bomb. Ronova replaced Alyosha after he walked into the storm and moved among the survivors in his body, nudging them to stage the events as a play.

Mitya carved her red eye into his hand. With it, he and the Traveler exposed "Alyosha". She snapped her fingers to send Odette and Chugunov to the Ley Lines ("That takes care of today's two"), then rewarded the survivors with answers. She explained that soothing lost souls is an angel's job, so she let the living defuse the bomb while the Ley Lines took two souls each night. She called it killing two birds with one stone. She admitted she had thoroughly enjoyed the drama.

Vodyanitsa's requiem threw off her count. Mitya and the Traveler attacked her disguise, and she told them they were powerless in her domain. The Traveler's Pyro cut through the false form, and everyone woke alive. The mark leaves Mitya's soul bearing a trace of her authority, so he remembers what happens while he is dead.

6.comment: Ronova: Paimon and the Armory Palace
6.content: When another experiment triggered the curse at the Armory Palace, Ronova found the Traveler at the scene of a second mass death. She warned them not to interfere in Snezhnaya's affairs, saying a Descender is exactly the lifeline a dying civilisation would cling to. Then she noticed Paimon and moved to take her. Pierro, waking early, blocked the blow. She said Paimon may be a creation of Celestia but holds none of its power or authority, that their obsession with her was baffling, and that she would reclaim "it" next time. As the dead began to revive, she left rather than let mortals see her form.

7.content:
In 7.1, as Mitya moved Mistilteinn equipment through Rankova Zorya, Ronova appeared, cast her curse and turned the town into a battlefield. The Traveler woke first and stalled her as Pierro had planned. Dainsleif and Pierro then joined the fight. Meanwhile the Tsaritsa, hosting Rhinedottir at Zapolyarny Palace, used six Gnoses to slow time around her guest. The resurrection window passed, Celestia detected the deaths, and Ronova's Authority of Death was reclaimed.

While waiting, she threatened the Traveler with the fate of the Third Descender's remains. She said she could kill them for good once Asmoday returned, once she had evidence for a conviction, or once the Heavenly Principles woke, and promised torment in the meantime. When the revival did not begin, she sensed something was wrong and tried to leave. Dainsleif snared her, Pierro struck with the Eye of the Fatui, and she insisted no mortal could survive that power. Stripped of her authority, she called them a conniving crew and said she was finished with restraint.

The Traveler combined every element to destroy her escape portal. Pierro brought down a vast elemental nail, at a heavy cost to his life force. The dust cleared over an empty crater with a portal closing. Snezhnaya celebrated victory, and Mistilteinn's restrictions were lifted. Pierro still warned that she might have escaped.

8.comment: Ronova: The Eitr and the Parting Gift
8.content:
Mortally wounded, Ronova emerged before the Nail of Retribution hanging over the Cryo Dragon's corpse. "She who controls death cannot know the experience of dying," she said, and now she did. She named humans, gods and a censored third party, and said she need not despise them any longer. She called on the Eitr, the "mother of all forbidden creations" that Hyperborea had hidden in the Shadow Realm, and fused it into the Nail. The Nail began to crumble, and she called it her parting gift.

The cinematic says she meant all Teyvat to feel what she felt as Holy Soil spread. Afterwards Nails of Retribution all across Teyvat began behaving strangely; the Snezhnayan one glows and periodically makes a sound. In Anomaly: Snezhnaya, Paimon wonders whether it is her revenge. This is the cliffhanger of 7.1, and nothing later is canon here.

9.comment: Ronova: Tuonetar of the Far North
9.content: The Frostmoon Scions' old hymns call her Tuonetar, a somber, fearsome mistress of the dead. She sees, hears and judges all, and no plea moves her, yet the hymn calls gentleness and mercy her first nature. At each autumn harvest, animals were burned in boat-shaped vessels for that year's dead, their eyes offered to her separately. Aila, the first Moonchanter, abolished the rite five centuries ago. Aila also claimed that the Lady of the Underworld guided her hand to end Lovia, though this rests on her word alone.

10.content: Rhinedottir is Ronova's partner in the Snezhnaya scheme: Ronova's curse kills, and Rhinedottir revives before Celestia notices. In the teaser, Ronova scolds her for leaving "bizarre creations" in others' spaces; it is Naberius, whose power Rhinedottir carries, whose nagging Rhinedottir says gets under her skin. In 7.1 Rhinedottir told the Tsaritsa that Ronova seems serious but is capricious, and that anyone should be grateful not to face her. Stalled in slowed time, Rhinedottir let the window lapse. Celestia then directed her to undo Ronova's killings, and she complied. Noting that Celestia was watching her and Naberius closely as likely accomplices, and that she did not want the Authority of Life reclaimed too, she declined to punish the Tsaritsa.

11.comment: Ronova: Pierro and the Eye of the Fatui
11.content: Pierro met her gaze during the cataclysm, and she recognised him when Istaroth showed her who was watching. His curse of immortality let him wake early and block her at the Armory Palace. In 7.1 he unveiled the "Eye of the Fatui", a newly completed Delusion never before tested in live combat, declaring that the Fatui would pay any price for the right to gaze upon the gods. Ronova insisted no mortal body or mind could withstand it. The final blow drained his life force, and Dainsleif says the battle took an exceptionally heavy toll on his mind and soul.
